findings.message: version field mapped with insertable=false/updatable=false and no @Version annotation — Hibernate will never perform optimistic locking checks on this entity.
findings.manualAction: Remove RewardBalance @Entity entirely (it is @Deprecated — migrate remaining callers to RewardWallet) OR add @Version to the version field and remove insertable=false/updatable=false.

findings.message: doCreditInTx and doCreditCompanyInTx use findForUpdate + orElseGet(save) with a window between the SELECT FOR UPDATE (which only locks existing rows) and the INSERT. Two concurrent first-credit calls can both find no row and both INSERT, hitting a unique constraint violation. Mitigation: WalletService.withOptimisticRetry catches DataIntegrityViolationException (23505) and retries — mitigated at service layer, but depends on the DB unique constraint existing.
findings.manualAction: Verify unique constraint on reward_wallets(client_id, user_id, currency_id, wallet_type) and reward_wallets(client_id, partner_company_id, currency_id, wallet_type) in migration SQL.

findings.message: reservedBalance and walletType fields mapped as insertable=false/updatable=false — silent write discard if code mutates these fields via RewardBalance.
findings.manualAction: Acceptable short-term since RewardBalance is @Deprecated. Migrate callers to RewardWallet to eliminate risk permanently.

findings.message: reserve(), debit(), release(), returnCredit() lacked @Transactional(NEVER) — asymmetry with credit() and creditCompany() meant ambient transactions could silently participate.

existsByRewardWalletId idempotency check is not atomic with the subsequent INSERT: two concurrent calls with the same referenceId can both pass the check before either commits, producing duplicate ledger entries. Full mitigation requires a DB unique constraint on ledger_entry(reward_wallet_id, reference_type, reference_id).
findings.manualAction: Add a unique DB constraint on ledger_entry(reward_wallet_id, reference_type, reference_id) and catch ConstraintViolationException as the idempotency guard. The application-level check is a best-effort defence only.

findings.message: amount parameter is not validated before arithmetic — null or non-positive values produce NullPointerException or silent economically-meaningless ledger entries.
findings.manualAction: Add Objects.requireNonNull(amount) and amount.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) > 0 guard at the top of each mutating method.

code-review.notes: 1 auto-fix (WalletService @Transactional(NEVER)). WalletMutationDelegate now reviewed. findings.summary: Retried non-credit wallet mutations can apply the same business event repeatedly
findings.details: reserve, debit, release, and returnCredit all accept referenceType/referenceId and append a ledger entry, but unlike credit they never check for an existing reference. The database unique index only covers entry_type = CREDIT. A caller retrying the same redemption settlement/cancel/return event with the same reference can move balances again.
findings.tierReason: alreadyHandled=true — all four non-credit mutations (doReserveInTx, doDebitInTx, doReleaseInTx, doReturnCreditInTx) now have the duplicate-reference guard matching the doCreditInTx pattern (commit e005011)
findings.recommendation: Add existsByRewardWalletIdAndReferenceTypeAndReferenceId check before balance mutation in all non-credit methods.

findings.summary: Budget-utilization unique indexes can fail migration on existing duplicate rows
findings.details: V9 adds partial unique indexes to budget_utilizations, but the baseline schema only had non-unique indexes. If production already has duplicate rows, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX aborts the Flyway migration and blocks deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add a pre-migration deduplication step before CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, or add explicit data-normalization to V9.
